findings.passage: As Secretary of State, he fought to implement a constitutional voter ID law requiring identification to cast a ballot. He also made it easier for our military servicemembers who are serving overseas to vote and helped clean up bloated voter rolls.
findings.note: Campaign site page (2023 re-election, says vote August 8); site text is written in the third person. Page itself is undated.

findings.passage:
Under Delbert’s leadership as Lt. Governor, the Mississippi Senate voted to:
Allow the Secretary of State to perform a full citizenship check to ensure illegal aliens are not voting;
findings.note: Campaign site list of Senate actions during his term as Lt. Governor; other items on the list cover paper-ballot equipment funds, tools for clerks to keep voter rolls accurate, and a ban on private money for running elections.

findings.passage: My record is what best qualifies me to serve as Lieutenant Governor. I have experience drafting and implementing meaningful legislation, like the bill securing insurance coverage for treatment for autism and other developmental disorders and Voter ID, and a history of bringing Mississippians with many different perspectives together to solve a problem.
findings.note: Written answer to a candidate questionnaire (verbatim responses per the paper); date is the original story date, republished by the Mississippi Free Press in 2025.

findings.passage: “Recent news articles have stated a provision of Mississippi’s Voter ID law, allowing a Mississippian to be issued a free voter identification card, has not been codified in state law. Those articles are inaccurate. The provision requiring a free Voter ID card is provided for in state law,” Hosemann said in a statement today.
findings.note: Statement as Lt. Governor, quoted by the Mississippi Free Press. The paper's text has non-breaking spaces and a line break inside the quote. He cites Miss. Code 23-15-7 on no fee for a voter ID card.

findings.passage: “To get those voter rolls right is important to the state—it’s important to the country,” Hosemann said.
findings.note: Quoted by the Mississippi Free Press (story dated 2021-01-30, says he spoke to the media on a Thursday); he said he supported action to clean up the voter rolls.

findings.passage: “Well, I’d like to think we had a relatively good Secretary of State for a while and one of the things we ran on 12 years ago now, was to implement a voter ID and have secure elections,” said Hosemann.
findings.note: Interview with Y'all Politics (Magnolia Tribune) as Lt. Governor, on how voter ID was put in place in Mississippi.

findings.passage: “I particularly didn’t want him to sue me. I remember it got dead quiet when I said that, at that time,” said Hosemann, telling Herrin, “Besides I had to get an ID to get in here to see you so I don’t see why you wouldn’t have one to vote.”
findings.note: Same interview; he recounts a meeting with a U.S. Justice Department official while planning the law. The article also says a 2012 exit survey found more than 98 percent of surveyed voters had a qualifying ID (reporter's words).

findings.passage: “Our office is taking a proactive, rather than reactive, approach to the constitutional change,” Hosemann said in a statement. “We are hoping to find as many people as possible who need a voter ID while we are awaiting approval. We can then expedite the process for getting them the proper identification later.”
findings.note: Statement as Secretary of State on free voter ID cards (paper says announced the day before its 2012-06-19 post; date is the day before the post).

findings.passage: “It’s a chance for the citizens to rise up and make a decision without the Legislature,” Hosemann said. “Now, because we didn’t(pass voter ID in the Legislautre), we’ve got to go through the initiative process. It takes a good bit of work.”
findings.note: Quoted by the Daily Leader (Brookhaven) on the voter ID ballot initiative while Secretary of State. Spelling and the bracket text are the paper's. Same story quotes him: "There is heavy activity and I think it will pick up during the summer months."

findings.passage: “The goal is not to exclude people from voting. The arguments that this would disenfranchise somebody are just wrong,” Hosemann said.
findings.note: Quoted by the Picayune Item (post dated 2008-01-31; says he met lawmakers on Tuesday) on his proposed voter ID requirement. Same story says he proposed that voters present a photo ID, a utility bill or a free ID from the Secretary of State (reporter's words).
